text.p: Aluminium nearby backwardations were the focus of attention during Monday afternoon LME trading, with increased cash/Sept tightness helping to stave off falls in forward prices.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau index fell 1.45 points to 237.68.

On the LME, aluminium prices bottomed out at $1,656 a tonne before closing at $1,677, still down $24 from Friday's kerb close. The cash/threes backwardation widened out to $55/60, due to the cash/Sept borrowing. On Friday, the benchmark spread was around $31.

Copper was again hit by liquidation, following on from last Friday, with prices dropping to near seven-month lows of $2,153 at one stage. Another rise in stocks, as well as the market being in a $4/6 cash/threes contango, underlined current negative sentiment. Last kerb trade was at $2,162, down $51.
Zinc prices fell under the $1,500 level during the afternoon sessions, briefly uncovering some sell-stops down to a low of $1,480 before last trade at $1,492, down $32.
Nickel prices fluctuated in a fairly wide band throughout, but were steadier for most of the session - a trend that reflected a heavily oversold market. Last business was at $6,670, up $40.
Tin was mostly quiet, closing at $5,370, down $10. Lead was generally routine as well, holding above $600, but still finishing $5 lower at $610. Alloy ended at a slightly lower $1,500/10.

CBOT soft red winter wheat futures posted modest gains on Monday amid concerns of weather problems in other major wheat growing countries, traders said. Wheat ended 3-1/2 to 1/2 cent per bushel higher with December up 3-1/4 at $3.72-3/4 a bushel.

IPE September Brent climbed well above lows where it languished for most of Monday to last trade just seven cents down at $18.92 a barrel, brokers said. "There was some short-covering towards the close but there is no real news out there," said one broker. Fears that the summer rally in U.S. gasoline markets was about to end tipped Brent lower earlier in the day and most trade was in the $18.75-$18.85 range. Weak unleaded futures and WTI held London values down after New York markets opened.

COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended sharply lower Monday, after a late sell-off, as the U.S. dollar and U.S. stocks and bonds recovered some ground. But the sell-off was led by bullion dealers and many traders are convinced another European central bank sell program is underway. COMEX December gold ended down $4.80 at $324.70 an ounce, after losing about $2.80 an ounce in the last half hour alone. Estimated final COMEX gold volume was only moderate at 31,000 lots, but about 9,000 lots were traded in the last hour. In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $321.10/60, compared to the London Monday afternoon fix at $322.60 and the New York close Friday around $325.80/30.
